sights.n: National Museum of the U.S. Air Force
sights.w: The marquee: world's largest and oldest military aviation museum, 4 hangars of aircraft from the Wright 1909 Military Flyer to an SR-71, XB-70 and presidential planes. Free admission, free parking, open daily 9-5.

65-acre Dayton History campus built around the original 1905 Wright Flyer III, the only airplane that is a National Historic Landmark, gifted by Orville Wright himself and shown in a purpose-built pit.
NPS-run bike shop where the Wright brothers designed and built the machines that led to the 1903 first flight; the anchor of Dayton Aviation Heritage NHP in the Wright-Dunbar district. Free.

The 84-acre pasture where the Wrights perfected controlled, powered flight in 1904-05 and ran the world's first flying school. NPS site on WPAFB, free, with an interpretive center at the Wright Memorial.

NPS visitor center in the Wrights' former print-shop building; tells the intertwined stories of Wilbur, Orville and their classmate, poet Paul Laurence Dunbar. Free, gateway to the Wright-Dunbar aviation trail.
Orville Wright's grand 1914 Oakwood mansion (a National Historic Landmark) where he lived until his death; toured by advance-reservation shuttle from Carillon Park on Wednesdays and Saturdays.
1930 Italian-Renaissance-villa art museum overlooking downtown, with 20,000+ works across 5,000 years; anchors the Grafton Hill bluff. Open Wed-Sun.
Reconstructed Fort Ancient (c. 1200 CE) Native American village and solar-calendar site on the Great Miami River, a National Historic Landmark now operated by Boonshoft; open seasonally.
Hands-on science-and-nature museum with a planetarium, small zoo and children's exhibits north of downtown; the region's top family science destination.
Downtown riverfront park at the Great Miami confluence: Five Rivers Fountain of Lights, splash pad, winter ice rink, kayak and bike rentals, and the hub of the region's paved trail network. Free.

Dayton's oldest neighborhood and nightlife heart: a quarter-mile of brick-lined East Fifth Street lined with bars, restaurants and shops, named an APA Great Street. Best-preserved 1820-1915 architecture in the city.
1904 Flemish-façade glass-domed arcade, a downtown landmark reborn after a $162M restoration wrapped in 2025 (Hilton Garden Inn, food hall, shops); the rotunda dome is the showpiece.

1841 garden cemetery and 200-acre arboretum on rolling hills; resting place of the Wright brothers, Paul Laurence Dunbar, Erma Bombeck and Charles Kettering, with a Tiffany-windowed Romanesque chapel. Free.
189-acre MetroPark of formal gardens, a butterfly house, edible-landscape and towering observation tower south of the city. Open daily, free.
17-foot pink-granite obelisk on Wright Brothers Hill (dedicated 1940 on Orville's birthday) with an overlook across Huffman Prairie and the Mad River valley. Free.
World's largest collection of Packard automobiles and memorabilia, displayed inside a beautifully restored original 1917 Packard dealership showroom downtown.

1850 Greek Revival courthouse modeled on the Temple of Hephaestus, on whose steps Lincoln gave an 1859 anti-slavery speech; now the Montgomery County Historical Society museum in Courthouse Square. Free.

sights.n: Paul Laurence Dunbar House Historic Site
sights.address: 219 Paul Laurence Dunbar St, Dayton, OH 45402
sights.w: 1904-06 home of pioneering Black poet Paul Laurence Dunbar, preserved with his belongings; Ohio's first state memorial to an African American (1936) and part of the aviation-heritage park.
1,000-acre preserve with 25 miles of trails, cascades and the iron-orange Yellow Spring that named the village; the day-trip centerpiece. $10 parking.
Dramatic dolomite-and-limestone gorge cut by the Little Miami River, a National Natural Landmark with cliff-edge trails; adjoins John Bryan State Park.
752-acre park called the most scenic in western Ohio, wrapping the Little Miami gorge with hiking, camping, rock climbing and a disc-golf course.
Paved rail-trail on a National Scenic River corridor; the Yellow Springs Station (old depot, restrooms, parking) is a favorite trailhead for an easy bike ride into the village and gorge.
National Audubon center with a working sustainable farm, prairies and woodland trails northwest of the city; a hands-on nature draw for families. Open Tue-Sun.
Downtown home of the Dayton Dragons, holders of pro sports' longest consecutive sellout streak (1,600+ games); a beloved summer-evening institution on Monument Avenue.
